title: The Fate of Boris and Brexit

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: As Britain holds its election, Boris Johnson is appealing to voters who believe that his promise to get Brexit done will mean restoring Britain to its past glory.
sentences.zh: 在英国举行大选之际，鲍里斯·约翰逊正在向选民呼吁，他承诺完成脱欧将意味着让英国恢复往日的辉煌。

sentences.en: My colleague Mark Landler on what it actually means.
sentences.zh: 我的同事马克·兰德勒将解读这到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, December 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: So Mark, you have been traveling around the UK in the days leading up to this general election.
sentences.zh: 马克，在大选前的几天里，你一直在英国各地奔波。

sentences.en: What is the feeling there?
sentences.zh: 那里的感觉如何？

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of strange, Michael, because on the one hand, this is a monumentally important election for the British people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，这感觉有点奇怪，因为一方面，这对英国人民来说是一场极其重要的大选。

sentences.en: And it was called in a very dramatic way back in late October by Boris Johnson.
sentences.zh: 而且它是由鲍里斯·约翰逊在10月下旬以一种非常戏剧性的方式宣布的。

sentences.en: Yet as the election has unfolded over the last six weeks, it's felt oddly
sentences.zh: 然而，随着过去六周选举的展开，它却让人感到莫名其妙地

sentences.en: anticlimactic.
sentences.zh: 虎头蛇尾。

sentences.en: I think some of this has to do with the time of the year.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与一年中的时间有关。

sentences.en: It gets dark really early in
sentences.zh: 在一年中的这个时候，英国

sentences.en: Britain at this time of the year.
sentences.zh: 天黑得非常早。

sentences.en: The weather's also cold.
sentences.zh: 天气也很冷。

sentences.en: And I think more importantly, the British people are really in the mood for Christmas.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为更重要的是，英国人民现在真的很想过圣诞节。

sentences.en: Christmas is just a huge holiday in this country.
sentences.zh: 圣诞节在这个国家是一个非常盛大的节日。

sentences.en: And so I think for that reason, rather than generating the kind of excitement, which sort of
sentences.zh: 所以我认为正是因为这个原因，人们并没有产生那种像美国大选那样

sentences.en: leads to a peak the way it would in an American election, you sort of have a kind of a surly electorate
sentences.zh: 推向高潮的兴奋感，反而出现了一种暴躁的选民群体，

sentences.en: that feels like they're being forced to think about these serious issues at a time when they ought to be decorating their tree and going to their kids' Christmas play.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得在应该装饰圣诞树、去看孩子们的圣诞演出时，却被迫去思考这些严肃的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Nothing says Christmas like a general election.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比大选更能代表圣诞节了。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And in fact, even from a logistical point of view, it's potentially problematic because
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使从后勤角度来看，这也可能存在问题，因为

sentences.en: some of the polling places that you would normally use in a general election are being reserved for
sentences.zh: 一些在大选中通常使用的投票站现在被预订用于

sentences.en: Christmas parties, nativity exhibits, plays, concerts.
sentences.zh: 圣诞派对、耶稣诞生展览、戏剧和音乐会。

sentences.en: So even from a purely practical point of view, it's not the best time of the year to hold an election.
sentences.zh: 所以即使从纯粹实际的角度来看，这也不是举行选举的最佳时机。

sentences.en: But you said that this is, in fact, a monumental election.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才说，这实际上是一场意义重大的选举。

sentences.en: So explain why that is.
sentences.zh: 那么请解释一下原因。

sentences.en: This is an election, correct me if I'm wrong, for prime minister.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，这是一场选出首相的选举。

sentences.en: It is not a vote for Brexit, right?
sentences.zh: 这不是对脱欧的投票，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, it isn't technically a vote for or against Brexit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从技术上讲，这并不是对脱欧与否的投票。

sentences.en: But in a way, it's a proxy for that vote.
sentences.zh: 但在某种程度上，它是那次投票的代理。

sentences.en: And to understand that, you need to go back to when Boris Johnson called this election and why he called it.
sentences.zh: 要理解这一点，你需要回到鲍里斯·约翰逊宣布这次选举的时间和原因。

sentences.en: Mr. Speaker, well, Mr. Speaker, I want to begin by echoing what you've just said.
sentences.zh: 议长先生，嗯，议长先生，我想先附和一下您刚才所说的话。

sentences.en: My gratitude to all members of the House for assembling on a Saturday for the first time in 37 years.
sentences.zh: 感谢议会所有成员37年来首次在周六齐聚一堂。

sentences.en: Back in September and October, after Boris Johnson had been elected prime minister by his own party, not by the general public.
sentences.zh: 回到9月和10月，在鲍里斯·约翰逊被他自己的政党而非公众选为首相之后。

sentences.en: He came in and he tried very aggressively to push through a plan to get
sentences.zh: 他上任后非常积极地推动一项计划，以完成

sentences.en: Brexit done, to get Britain out of the European Union.
sentences.zh: 脱欧，让英国退出欧盟。

sentences.en: Let's go for a deal that can heal this country and can allow us all to express our legitimate desires for the deepest possible friendship and partnership with our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 让我们达成一项能够治愈这个国家，并让我们所有人都能表达与邻国建立尽可能深厚的友谊与伙伴关系的合法愿望的协议。

sentences.en: And a deal that also allows us to believe in ourselves once again as an open, generous, global, outward looking, free-trading United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这项协议也让我们能够再次相信自己是一个开放、慷慨、全球化、目光远大、自由贸易的联合王国。

sentences.en: That is the prospect.
sentences.zh: 这就是前景。

sentences.en: The problem is he didn't have a working majority.
sentences.zh: 问题是他没有获得有效多数席位。

sentences.en: So every time he tried to do this, he was stymied both by the opposition and by breakaway members of his own conservative party.
sentences.zh: 所以每当他试图这样做时，都会受到反对派和他自己保守党内分裂成员的阻挠。

sentences.en: The eyes to the right, 308.
sentences.zh: 赞成票308张。

sentences.en: The nose to the left, 322.
sentences.zh: 反对票322张。

sentences.en: And so he decided at the end of October to force through a general election to throw this back to
sentences.zh: 因此，他在10月底决定强行举行大选，将这个问题重新抛给

sentences.en: the British people on the calculation that if they gave him a solid majority, he would then have a free hand to deliver Brexit.
sentences.zh: 英国人民，他的算盘是，如果他们给他一个稳固的多数席位，他就能放手去实现脱欧。

sentences.en: I don't want an early election and no one much wants to have an election in December, but we've got to the stage where we have no choice.
sentences.zh: 我不想要提前选举，也没人想在12月进行选举，但我们已经到了别无选择的地步。

sentences.en: So while it is in fact an election for control of the Parliament, it is at some very fundamental level a vote for or against Boris Johnson's Brexit.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然这实际上是一场争夺议会控制权的选举，但在某种根本层面上，这是对鲍里斯·约翰逊脱欧方案的赞成或反对票。

sentences.en: I'm going out now to campaign across the whole country.
sentences.zh: 我现在要出去在全国范围内进行竞选活动。

sentences.en: Let's get Brexit done and unleash the potential of the whole United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 让我们完成脱欧，释放整个联合王国的潜力。

sentences.en: So, Mork, how is Boris Johnson selling this election, kind of this desperate Hail Mary play of an election to the voters?
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，鲍里斯·约翰逊是如何向选民推销这场选举的，这种孤注一掷的选举？

sentences.en: What is he saying?
sentences.zh: 他在说什么？

sentences.en: How is he talking about it?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么谈论这件事的？

sentences.en: Well, he's selling it with three words.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他用三个词来推销它。

sentences.en: Get Brexit done.
sentences.zh: 完成脱欧。

sentences.en: It's an incredibly simple, single-minded, narrow message.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其简单、专注且狭隘的信息。

sentences.en: It says to the British voters, you guys are sick and tired of hearing about this.
sentences.zh: 它告诉英国选民，你们已经听腻了这件事。

sentences.en: We're sick and tired of debating it.
sentences.zh: 我们也已经辩论腻了。

sentences.en: I am the leader who will get Brexit done so Britain can move on to whatever its next chapter is.
sentences.zh: 我就是那个能完成脱欧的领导人，这样英国就能进入下一个篇章。

sentences.en: Get Brexit done.
sentences.zh: 完成脱欧。

sentences.en: And we can restore confidence and certainty to business and to families.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能恢复商业和家庭的信心与确定性。

sentences.en: It's an extremely simple message.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其简单的信息。

sentences.en: It's one that he's hammered away at every single day of this election, almost to the exclusion of any other topic.
sentences.zh: 他在这次选举的每一天都在反复强调这一点，几乎排除了任何其他话题。

sentences.en: Get Brexit done and we can focus our hearts and our minds on the priorities of the British people.
sentences.zh: 完成脱欧，我们就能把精力和心思集中在英国人民的优先事项上。

sentences.en: I've been following Boris Johnson for the last few weeks on the campaign trail.
sentences.zh: 过去几周我一直在竞选活动中跟随鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: And the other day, I was up in Staffordshire, where Prime
sentences.zh: 前几天，我在斯塔福德郡，约翰逊首相

sentences.en: Minister Johnson appeared at a factory that makes giant construction equipment.
sentences.zh: 出现在一家制造大型建筑设备工厂。

sentences.en: They built a brick wall out of styrofoam.
sentences.zh: 他们用泡沫塑料砌了一堵砖墙。

sentences.en: They wrote the word gridlock across it in giant red letters.
sentences.zh: 他们在上面用巨大的红色字母写着“僵局”这个词。

sentences.en: And then Boris Johnson drove a backhoe through the styrofoam wall.
sentences.zh: 然后鲍里斯·约翰逊开着挖掘机撞穿了那堵泡沫塑料墙。

sentences.en: The shovel on the backhoe said, get Brexit done.
sentences.zh: 挖掘机的铲斗上写着“完成脱欧”。

sentences.en: And there was a giant Union Jack on the back.
sentences.zh: 后面还有一个巨大的英国国旗。

sentences.en: That is very subtle.
sentences.zh: 这非常含蓄。

sentences.en: I think it is time for the whole country, symbolically, to get in the cab.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在是整个国家象征性地坐进驾驶室的时候了。

sentences.en: It's about as blunt as you can get.
sentences.zh: 这已经够直白了。

sentences.en: And remove the current blockage that we have in our parliamentary system.
sentences.zh: 并消除我们议会系统中目前的阻碍。

sentences.en: And it aptly summarizes what his whole campaign has been about, which is that dysfunction and paralysis and gridlock exist in Westminster, exist in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 它恰如其分地总结了他整个竞选活动的主旨，即威斯敏斯特和议会中存在功能失调、瘫痪和僵局。

sentences.en: And I'm the one guy that can smash my way through it, can bulldoze my way through to this bright future for Britain.
sentences.zh: 而我就是那个能冲破阻碍、能推土机般开辟英国光明未来的人。

sentences.en: 48 hours to end the deadlock.
sentences.zh: 还有48小时结束僵局。

sentences.en: 48 hours to end the gridlock.
sentences.zh: 还有48小时结束停滞。

sentences.en: The...
sentences.zh: 那个……

sentences.en: Think of another word.
sentences.zh: 再想一个词。

sentences.en: Deadlock, gridlock.
sentences.zh: 僵局，停滞。

sentences.en: As long as you elect me and the Conservative Party.
sentences.zh: 只要你们选我和保守党。

sentences.en: Roadblock.
sentences.zh: 路障。

sentences.en: 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 48小时。

sentences.en: And is he right about the simplicity of this?
sentences.zh: 他关于这种简单性的说法对吗？

sentences.en: If you elect me, Brexit gets done.
sentences.zh: 如果你选我，脱欧就会完成。

sentences.en: Well, at one level, it is just as simple as that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从一个层面来看，确实就是这么简单。

sentences.en: If Boris Johnson emerges from this election with even a single-seat majority, he will be able to deliver on his promise to leave the European
sentences.zh: 如果鲍里斯·约翰逊在这次选举中哪怕以一个席位的多数获胜，他就能实现他在明年一月底前离开欧盟的承诺。

sentences.en: Union at the end of next January.
sentences.zh: 欧盟。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But I think what the British public doesn't fully understand is that that's not the end of the story.
sentences.zh: 但我认为英国公众并没有完全理解，这并不是故事的终点。

sentences.en: That's really just the end of Act 1.
sentences.zh: 这实际上只是第一幕的结束。

sentences.en: So what happens in Act 2?
sentences.zh: 那么第二幕会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, Boris Johnson has negotiated a deal to leave the European Union.
sentences.zh: 嗯，鲍里斯·约翰逊已经谈妥了一项脱欧协议。

sentences.en: But now he immediately has to turn around and negotiate a new permanent trade agreement with the European Union.
sentences.zh: 但现在他必须立即转过身来，与欧盟谈判一项新的永久性贸易协定。

sentences.en: The only difference is the first time he was negotiating with Brussels, Britain was still a member of the EU.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别是，他第一次与布鲁塞尔谈判时，英国还是欧盟成员国。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now Britain's going to be negotiating with the EU as an outsider.
sentences.zh: 现在英国将以局外人的身份与欧盟谈判。

sentences.en: So it's going to be a very, very difficult negotiation, one that under the rules, he has to finish by the end of 2020.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一场非常、非常艰难的谈判，按照规则，他必须在2020年底前完成。

sentences.en: And if he fails to do that, then Britain and the EU head into very uncharted territory with no agreement covering how they trade with each other.
sentences.zh: 如果他失败了，那么英国和欧盟将进入一个非常未知的领域，没有任何协议涵盖他们如何进行贸易。

sentences.en: But truth in advertising, he is accurate.
sentences.zh: 但从广告的真实性来说，他是准确的。

sentences.en: If you vote for Boris Johnson, if you vote for the conservatives, then the long national nightmare of Brexit not really ever happening.
sentences.zh: 如果你投票给鲍里斯·约翰逊，如果你投票给保守党，那么脱欧从未真正发生的漫长国家噩梦就结束了。

sentences.en: That ends.
sentences.zh: 结束了。

sentences.en: Actually, I'm not quite sure that's the case.
sentences.zh: 其实，我不确定情况是否如此。

sentences.en: Brexit defined purely as Britain leaves the European Union.
sentences.zh: 如果将脱欧纯粹定义为英国离开欧盟。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是对的。

sentences.en: That would be accomplished if Boris Johnson wins this election.
sentences.zh: 如果鲍里斯·约翰逊赢得这次选举，那将得以实现。

sentences.en: But if you define Brexit as Britain finding a new place in the world, a new relationship with its most important neighbor, Europe, then it's not truth in advertising.
sentences.zh: 但如果你将脱欧定义为英国在世界上找到新的位置，与最重要的邻居欧洲建立新的关系，那么这就不完全是真实的广告了。

sentences.en: That part of the drama is still to unfold.
sentences.zh: 那部分剧情还有待展开。

sentences.en: And that's where I think the debate and the message that Boris Johnson has been giving to voters is not quite the complete one.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为鲍里斯·约翰逊给选民的辩论和信息并不完全完整。

sentences.en: Pesky reporters always complicating these three word bumper stickers.
sentences.zh: 讨厌的记者总是让这些三个词的竞选口号变得复杂。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, that's the nature of bumper stickers, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是竞选口号的本质，对吧？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So what's the other option for voters?
sentences.zh: 那么选民还有什么其他选择？

sentences.en: What is the Labour Party's pitch on the other side of this debate?
sentences.zh: 工党在辩论的另一方有什么主张？

sentences.en: Well, if you think of Boris Johnson's pitch as being very simple and very clear, the Labour Party's position is the opposite.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你认为鲍里斯·约翰逊的推销非常简单明了，那么工党的立场恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's in some ways quite muddled.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，它相当混乱。

sentences.en: What the Labour Party is saying is, elect us and we will go negotiate a new withdrawal agreement with Brussels.
sentences.zh: 工党所说的是，选我们，我们将去与布鲁塞尔谈判一项新的脱欧协议。

sentences.en: We'll bring that agreement back and we will then throw it back to the public and let the public vote.
sentences.zh: 我们将带回该协议，然后将其交还给公众，让公众投票。

sentences.en: So if you vote for Labour, what you are in effect voting for is a second referendum on whether to leave Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你投票给工党，你实际上是在投票支持第二次关于是否离开欧洲的公投。

sentences.en: So at some level, if you're a Remainer, if your goal is to stay in the European Union, this is your last chance.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，如果你是留欧派，如果你的目标是留在欧盟，这是你最后的机会。

sentences.en: So this is the exact opposite of a bumper sticker slogan.
sentences.zh: 所以这与竞选口号完全相反。

sentences.en: It's kind of a muddle.
sentences.zh: 这有点混乱。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's very complicated for an electorate that is tired, fed up, has been listening to the Brexit debate for three and a half years and just desperately wants to move on.
sentences.zh: 是的，对于一个疲惫不堪、受够了、已经听了三年半脱欧辩论并迫切想要继续前进的选民群体来说，这非常复杂。

sentences.en: And so the Labour Party's had a very hard time making this an attractive pitch out on the campaign trail.
sentences.zh: 所以工党在竞选活动中很难让这个主张变得有吸引力。

sentences.en: Our leader, the next prime minister, Jeremy Corbyn.
sentences.zh: 我们的领袖，下一任首相，杰里米·科尔宾。

sentences.en: And that's why you've seen Labour Party leaders and candidates talk about almost anything else.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你看到工党领袖和候选人谈论几乎任何其他事情。

sentences.en: This election is now a fight for the survival of our National Health Service as a public service free for all at the point of need.
sentences.zh: 这次选举现在是一场为了我们国家医疗服务体系作为一项在需要时人人免费的公共服务的生存而战。

sentences.en: They talk about kitchen table issues.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是民生问题。

sentences.en: Voters need to ask themselves some very serious questions.
sentences.zh: 选民需要问自己一些非常严肃的问题。

sentences.en: Is the NHS safe in Boris Johnson's hands?
sentences.zh: 英国国家医疗服务体系在鲍里斯·约翰逊手中安全吗？

sentences.en: Like the state of Britain's National Health Service, the crime levels in the cities, funding for education.
sentences.zh: 比如英国国家医疗服务体系的状况、城市的犯罪水平、教育经费等。

sentences.en: We will create a national education service, make lifelong education a right.
sentences.zh: 我们将建立国家教育服务体系，让终身教育成为一项权利。

sentences.en: Really almost anything aside from the core issue in the campaign, which is Brexit.
sentences.zh: 除了竞选的核心议题——脱欧之外，几乎所有其他议题都无关紧要。

sentences.en: And yes, let's be clear, we will scrap university tuition fees.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们要明确一点，我们将废除大学学费。

sentences.en: So they're trying to run a traditional campaign when in reality it sounds like that's not exactly where voters' minds are.
sentences.zh: 所以他们试图开展一场传统的竞选活动，但实际上，选民们关心的似乎并非如此。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they're also trying to run this traditional campaign against an opponent, Boris Johnson, who is stubbornly unwilling to engage them on any of these other issues.
sentences.zh: 他们还试图针对鲍里斯·约翰逊这位对手开展这种传统竞选，而约翰逊固执地不愿在这些议题上与他们交锋。

sentences.en: There was a really vivid example of this just a few days ago on the campaign trail.
sentences.zh: 就在几天前，竞选活动中出现了一个非常生动的例子。

sentences.en: The picture that broke hearts and triggered one of the more important disputes of this election, a four-year-old boy.
sentences.zh: 那张令人心碎的照片引发了本次选举中最重要的争议之一，照片里是一个四岁的小男孩。

sentences.en: There was this very harrowing case of a young boy who was sick and had been brought to an emergency room at a hospital in Leeds.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人揪心的案例，一名小男孩生病了，被送到了利兹一家医院的急诊室。

sentences.en: This hospital was overcrowded.
sentences.zh: 这家医院人满为患。

sentences.en: There was no bed for him.
sentences.zh: 没有床位给他。

sentences.en: And so the boy went to sleep on the floor in the waiting room and people snapped pictures of him.
sentences.zh: 于是男孩只能睡在候诊室的地板上，人们拍下了他的照片。

sentences.en: Well, a local reporter confronted Boris Johnson on the campaign trail.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一位当地记者在竞选活动中质问了鲍里斯·约翰逊。

sentences.en: What was your reaction when you saw that shocking picture of Jack Willamette, the four-year-old?
sentences.zh: 当你看到那张四岁男孩杰克·威拉米特令人震惊的照片时，你的反应是什么？

sentences.en: With his phone in his hand, with a picture of this little boy on it.
sentences.zh: 他手里拿着手机，上面显示着这个小男孩的照片。

sentences.en: This is a photo.
sentences.zh: 这是一张照片。

sentences.en: This is a photo.
sentences.zh: 这是一张照片。

sentences.en: We need to be making...
sentences.zh: 我们需要做出……

sentences.en: And said, you know, Mr. Johnson, what do you say to the family of this boy?
sentences.zh: 并说，你知道，约翰逊先生，你对这个男孩的家人有什么想说的吗？

sentences.en: This is a four-year-old boy, Prime Minister, suspected of pneumonia, forced to lie on the floor on a pile of coats.
sentences.zh: 总理先生，这是一个四岁的小男孩，疑似患有肺炎，却被迫躺在地上的一堆外套上。

sentences.en: Isn't it unacceptable in this society that there isn't a hospital bed for someone like this?
sentences.zh: 在这个社会里，像这样的人连一张病床都没有，难道不令人无法接受吗？

sentences.en: Boris Johnson did not want to get drawn into the conversation.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·约翰逊不想被卷入这场谈话。

sentences.en: And that's why we're putting the records investment into the NHS now.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们现在要对国民医疗服务体系（NHS）进行创纪录的投资。

sentences.en: And finally, out of frustration, when the reporter wouldn't give up.
sentences.zh: 最后，由于记者不肯罢休，他感到很沮丧。

sentences.en: You refuse to look at the photo.
sentences.zh: 你拒绝看这张照片。

sentences.en: You've taken my phone, put it in your pocket, Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 总理先生，你拿走了我的手机，把它放进了你的口袋里。

sentences.en: He took the reporter's phone out of his hands and put it in his pocket.
sentences.zh: 他从记者手中夺过手机，放进了自己的口袋。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It was a really indelible image.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个难以磨灭的画面。

sentences.en: It sort of played to the Labour Party critique that Boris Johnson is uncaring, unfeeling, doesn't understand the problems of ordinary people.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上印证了工党的批评，即鲍里斯·约翰逊冷漠无情，不了解普通民众的问题。

sentences.en: And in a campaign that has sort of lacked for vivid images, it was perhaps the most memorable image for what has otherwise been a very disciplined campaign by the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 在这一场缺乏生动形象的竞选活动中，这或许是最令人难忘的画面，而除此之外，首相的竞选一直非常严谨。

sentences.en: Well, so, Mark, I'm curious how all this is playing out with British voters.
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，我很好奇这一切在英国选民中产生了怎样的影响。

sentences.en: On the one hand, it's very easy to understand why voters would be exhausted and desperate to put Brexit behind them, just get this thing over with.
sentences.zh: 一方面，很容易理解为什么选民会感到疲惫，迫切希望把脱欧抛在脑后，只想尽快结束这件事。

sentences.en: On the other hand, I could understand plenty of British voters saying, let's not rush to do this and therefore side with the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我能理解许多英国选民会说，让我们不要急于求成，因此站在工党一边。

sentences.en: That's right, and that's why this election is leading to potentially some very striking realignments in British politics.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是为什么这次选举可能会导致英国政坛出现一些非常惊人的重组。

sentences.en: Look at what the Conservative Party's strategy is and who they're going after in the electorate.
sentences.zh: 看看保守党的策略是什么，以及他们的目标选民是谁。

sentences.en: Their main target is a swath of working class voters across the Midlands and the industrial north of England.
sentences.zh: 他们的主要目标是中部地区和英格兰工业北部的大批工人阶级选民。

sentences.en: These are voters who, by custom, by tradition, have always voted for the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 这些选民按照习惯和传统，一直以来都投票给工党。

sentences.en: But in 2016, this slice of voters voted to leave the European Union, and they're increasingly fed up that their politicians haven't made that happen.
sentences.zh: 但在2016年，这部分选民投票支持脱离欧盟，他们越来越厌倦政客们迟迟未能实现这一目标。

sentences.en: So Boris Johnson has gone after these voters.
sentences.zh: 所以鲍里斯·约翰逊盯上了这些选民。

sentences.en: He is trying to appeal to them.
sentences.zh: 他试图争取他们的支持。

sentences.en: He's trying to convert these dozens of seats that have been in Labour hands for decades, some of them forever, into Conservative seats.
sentences.zh: 他试图将这些几十年来——有些甚至是永远——掌握在工党手中的几十个席位，转化为保守党的席位。

sentences.en: And if he does that, he will have, in effect, torn down what's known as the Red Wall.
sentences.zh: 如果他做到了，他实际上就推倒了所谓的“红墙”。

sentences.en: This is the wall of Labour strongholds that runs right across the middle of England.
sentences.zh: 这是一道横跨英格兰中部、由工党铁票仓组成的墙。

sentences.en: In the south of England, you actually have a reverse situation.
sentences.zh: 在英格兰南部，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The south of England is more prosperous than the north, and voters in the south have historically and by custom tended to vote more for the Conservative Party.
sentences.zh: 英格兰南部比北部更繁荣，南部的选民在历史上和习惯上倾向于更多地投票给保守党。

sentences.en: These are also voters who, in the main, voted to stay in the European Union in 2016.
sentences.zh: 这些选民在2016年也大多投票支持留在欧盟。

sentences.en: And they're really worried about their own party leader's determination to get Brexit done.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很担心他们自己的党魁完成脱欧的决心。

sentences.en: They worry about the consequences of that.
sentences.zh: 他们担心这样做的后果。

sentences.en: They worry that he's moving too faSt.
sentences.zh: 他们担心他动作太快了。

sentences.en: So even though their loyalties, by instinct and family tradition, are to vote for the Conservatives, they're having second thoughts.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管他们的直觉和家族传统让他们倾向于投票给保守党，但他们现在开始犹豫了。

sentences.en: And the Labour Party is making a play for these voters on the argument that this is your last chance to stay in Europe.
sentences.zh: 而工党正在争取这些选民，理由是这是你们留在欧洲的最后机会。

sentences.en: So this election could lead to this fascinating flipping of the map in England,
sentences.zh: 所以这次选举可能会导致英格兰政治版图出现这种迷人的翻转，

sentences.en: where the north and the Midlands would actually turn Conservative blue, while the south might turn more Labour red.
sentences.zh: 北部和中部地区实际上会变成保守党的蓝色，而南部可能会变成更多的工党红色。

sentences.en: And even beyond the enormous consequences of Brexit, you could see this election produce a new alignment in British politics.
sentences.zh: 即使抛开脱欧带来的巨大后果，你也可以看到这次选举在英国政坛产生了一种新的格局。

sentences.en: And Mark, what would that mean, that the Brexit question could actually flip party identifications in these two very important regions of Britain?
sentences.zh: 马克，如果脱欧问题真的能翻转英国这两个非常重要地区的政党认同，那意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think what's most important is that the Conservative Party would inherit many of these older, working class, formerly Labour voters in the industrial Midlands and North,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为最重要的是，保守党将继承工业中部和北部地区许多年长的、工人阶级的、曾经支持工党的选民，

sentences.en: who voted for Brexit, who voted for Brexit largely because they felt it would be a return to the Britain of their childhood,
sentences.zh: 他们投票支持脱欧，很大程度上是因为他们觉得这会让英国回到他们童年的样子，

sentences.en: the Britain of the 60s and 70s, an old-fashioned economy with heavy industry,
sentences.zh: 回到六七十年代的英国，一个拥有重工业的旧式经济体，

sentences.en: that it would cut off the flow of immigrants that are changing the way the main streets and their villages look,
sentences.zh: 他们认为这会切断改变了他们街道和村庄面貌的移民潮，

sentences.en: that it would really bring back a kind of a nostalgic view of Middle England.
sentences.zh: 这真的会带回一种对英格兰中部地区的怀旧情怀。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Make Britain great again.
sentences.zh: 让英国再次伟大。

sentences.en: Make Britain great again.
sentences.zh: 让英国再次伟大。

sentences.en: The analogies to Trump are extremely parallel.
sentences.zh: 这与特朗普的类比极其相似。

sentences.en: The big problem here is that that is not the vision that Boris Johnson and his closest advisers have for a Britain after Brexit.
sentences.zh: 这里最大的问题是，这并不是鲍里斯·约翰逊及其核心顾问对脱欧后英国的愿景。

sentences.en: The politicians like to talk about this new Britain as being something more akin to Singapore.
sentences.zh: 政客们喜欢谈论这个新英国，认为它更像新加坡。

sentences.en: They even have a phrase for it.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至为此创造了一个短语。

sentences.en: They call it Singapore on Thames.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为“泰晤士河畔的新加坡”。

sentences.en: And what that means is a country that is extremely open to foreign trade that becomes a kind of a magnet for highly educated,
sentences.zh: 这意味着一个对外国贸易极其开放的国家，成为吸引高学历、

sentences.en: highly skilled people, a place that has very light regulation, a fundamentally open economy.
sentences.zh: 高技能人才的磁石，一个监管非常宽松、本质上开放的经济体。

sentences.en: This is not at all what these new Conservative voters are going to be signing up for.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是这些新保守党选民所期待的。

sentences.en: They want the Britain of 1960, not the Britain of 2020.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是1960年的英国，而不是2020年的英国。

sentences.en: And I think the challenge for the Conservative Party, if they succeed on Election Day, is how they reconcile their own ambitions for Singapore on Thames
sentences.zh: 我认为保守党如果能在选举日取得成功，他们面临的挑战是如何调和他们自己对“泰晤士河畔新加坡”的雄心，

sentences.en: with the Middle England dreams of the voters that they brought into their fold over the course of this election.
sentences.zh: 与他们在这次选举中拉拢过来的选民对英格兰中部的梦想。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be an extremely difficult challenge for them to meet.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对他们来说将是一个极其艰巨的挑战。

sentences.en: So there's a very real possibility that voters will be lured to the Conservative Party today on a promise that Brexit is going to happen finally.
sentences.zh: 所以，选民今天因为“脱欧终于要实现了”的承诺而被吸引到保守党，这种可能性是非常真实的。

sentences.en: But they're not going to actually get a version of Britain that they envisioned or that they wanted or that is actually hospitable to them.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上并不会得到他们所设想、所渴望的，或者真正适合他们的英国版本。

sentences.en: I like to think of Brexit as a tale of two hangovers.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把脱欧看作是两个宿醉的故事。

sentences.en: The immediate hangover is when the British people realize that Brexit is not actually finished, that they're just embarking on the second act of this drama.
sentences.zh: 即时的宿醉是当英国人民意识到脱欧并没有真正完成，他们只是刚刚踏入这场戏的第二幕时。

sentences.en: The longer term hangover is when the people who voted for Brexit realize that the country they yearned for,
sentences.zh: 长期的宿醉是当那些投票支持脱欧的人意识到他们所向往的国家，

sentences.en: the restoration to an older Middle England, is not going to happen either.
sentences.zh: 那个恢复到旧日英格兰中部的愿景，也不会实现时。

sentences.en: That, in fact, the vision for this country is antithetical to what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个国家的愿景与他们想要的背道而驰。

sentences.en: It's a very different country than the one they grew up in.
sentences.zh: 这是一个与他们成长过程中完全不同的国家。

sentences.en: And that change is irrevocable.
sentences.zh: 而这种改变是不可逆转的。

sentences.en: Brexit was not ever going to bring back that future.
sentences.zh: 脱欧永远不可能带回那个未来。

sentences.en: And Boris Johnson certainly has no plans to bring it back.
sentences.zh: 而鲍里斯·约翰逊当然也没有计划带回它。

sentences.en: So that's the conundrum that the government's going to face and the British public is going to face as they navigate their way through this process.
sentences.zh: 这就是政府和英国公众在这一过程中所面临的难题。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Well, polls show that Boris Johnson's Conservative Party has a consistent lead heading into today's election and is likely to win a majority in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，鲍里斯·约翰逊的保守党在今天的选举中保持领先，很可能在议会中获得多数席位。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Please bear in mind this complex situation and the challenge to sovereignty and security in our country
sentences.zh: 请在评估那些试图处理叛乱的人的意图时，

sentences.en: when you are assessing the intent of those who attempted to deal with the rebellion.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这种复杂的情况以及对我国主权和安全的挑战。

sentences.en: Surely, under the circumstances, genocidal intent cannot be the only hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，种族灭绝意图肯定不是唯一的假设。

sentences.en: In testimony before the International Court of Justice on Wednesday, the leader of Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi, defended her government against charges that had carried out genocide
sentences.zh: 周三，缅甸领导人昂山素季在国际法院作证时，为她的政府辩护，反驳了有关其对国内罗兴亚穆斯林实施种族灭绝的指控，并表示外界未能理解局势的复杂性。

sentences.en: against Rohingya Muslims in her country and said that outsiders had failed to understand the complexity of the situation.
sentences.zh: 他们将妇女和儿童与男子分开，并有系统地杀害了男子。

sentences.en: They separated women and children from the men and systematically killed the men.
sentences.zh: 她的言论发表之前，证人讲述了缅甸军方对罗兴亚人施加的恐怖暴行，

sentences.en: Her remarks followed gruesome testimony from witnesses about the horrors inflicted on the Rohingya by Myanmar's military,
sentences.zh: 包括大规模处决、系统性强奸和数百个村庄被烧毁的指控。

sentences.en: including claims of mass executions, systematic rape, and the burning of hundreds of villages.
sentences.zh: 一位证人叙述道，

sentences.en: A witness recounted,
sentences.zh: 第一轮射击就像雨点般的子弹。

sentences.en: The first round of shooting was like a rain of bullets.
sentences.zh: 第二轮射击很慢，士兵们逐个杀害了那些男子。

sentences.en: The second round was slow, as the soldiers killed the men individually.
sentences.zh: 1991年因在缅甸的工作而获得诺贝尔和平奖的昂山素季，一直拒绝批评该国将军对待罗兴亚人的行为，

sentences.en: Aung San Suu Kyi, who won a Nobel Peace Prize in 1991 for her work in Myanmar, has consistently refused to criticize her country's generals for their conduct toward the Rohingya,
sentences.zh: 这引起了国际社会的谴责。

sentences.en: drawing international condemnation.
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，哈维·温斯坦及其前电影制片厂董事会

sentences.en: And, the Times reports that Harvey Weinstein and the board of his former film studio
sentences.zh: 已与数十名声称遭受他性侵的受害者初步达成2500万美元的和解协议。

sentences.en: have tentatively reached a $25 million settlement with dozens of alleged victims of his sexual assault.
sentences.zh: 该和解协议不要求温斯坦承认不当行为，也不要求他本人向受害者支付任何费用，因为这笔钱将由保险公司提供。

sentences.en: The settlement would not require Weinstein to admit wrongdoing or pay anything to the victims himself, since the money would be provided by insurance companies.
sentences.zh: 但这将结束针对他和他的前公司几乎所有的诉讼。

sentences.en: But it would bring to an end nearly every lawsuit against him and his former company.
sentences.zh: 温斯坦仍定于下个月因性侵两名女性的刑事指控受审。

sentences.en: Weinstein is still scheduled to go on trial next month on criminal charges of sexually assaulting two women.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
